items.q: Good morning! How are you?
items.a: I’m fine, thanks. How are you?
items.note: formal

items.q: Hello! How are you doing?
items.a: Fine, just fine. How are you?
items.note: informal

items.q: Hi, how is it going?
items.a: Pretty good. How about you?
items.note: informal

items.q: Hi, what’s up?
items.a: Not much. What about you?
items.note: informal

items.q: What have you been up to?
items.a: The same as usual.
items.note: informal

items.q: Thank you for looking after my son.
items.a: You’re very welcome.

items.q: Thanks for your help.
items.a: No problem.

items.q: Thank you for carrying my bag.
items.a: Don’t mention it.

items.q: That’s very kind of you but you really shouldn’t have gone to all this trouble.
items.a: I was happy to help.
items.note: you shouldn't have gone to all this trouble = standard phrase to someone who worked hard for you

items.q: Sorry to have kept you waiting.
items.a: That’s ok.

items.q: Sorry I’m late.
items.a: No problem. I’ve only just got here myself.

items.q: I’m sorry about reading your messages.
items.a: Don’t let it happen again.
items.note: don’t let it happen again = I hope you won't do this again

topics.title: How to ask people to do something for you

items.q: Could you open the window, please?
items.a: Sure.

items.q: Could you make me a cup of tea, please?
items.a: Yes, of course.

items.q: Could you give me his phone number, please?
items.a: I’m sorry but I don’t know his number.

items.q: Could you look after my son tonight?
items.a: I’m afraid I can’t. I’m working an evening shift today.
items.note: shift work = the time period during which you are at work

items.q: Do you mind moving your seat so that I and my friend could sit together?
items.a: No, of course not. (positive answer)

items.q: Do you mind lending me some money?
items.a: I’m sorry, I’m broke.
items.note: to be broke = to have no money

items.q: My flight arrives at 7 am.
items.a: Would you like me to meet you at the airport?

items.q: My car is broken, so I came to work by underground today.
items.a: Do you want me to give you a lift home?
items.note: to give a lift = to take someone somewhere in your car

items.q: The suitcase is so heavy.
items.a: Let me carry it for you!

items.q: What do these statistics mean?
items.a: Let me explain.

topics.title: How to ask for permission to do something

items.q: Can I switch the TV on?
items.a: Sure, go ahead.

items.q: Can I read this e-mail?
items.a: No, I’m afraid not.

items.q: Do you mind if I sit here?
items.a: No, of course not.

items.q: Do you mind if I borrow your car tomorrow?
items.a: Yes, I’m afraid I do.
items.note: to borrow = use another's item and return it later

topics.title: How to suggest somebody an idea

items.q: It’s hot in here.
items.a: Let’s open the window. — Okay.

items.q: Let’s ask your mum to look after Johnny while we are away.
items.a: I’d rather not.

items.q: How about going there by train?
items.a: Sounds good!

items.q: How about painting the walls blue?
items.a: It doesn’t sound very good.

items.q: Why don’t we go to the beach?
items.a: Good idea!

items.q: Why don’t you get a new hairstyle?
items.a: I don’t feel like it.

topics.title: How to agree and disagree with your companion

items.q: Kevin is musically gifted.
items.a: That’s true!
items.note: gifted = talented

items.q: I think Martin Freeman is a brilliant actor!
items.a: Absolutely!

items.q: The facts he gave us are convincing.
items.a: I can’t see that!
items.note: convincing = making you believe it is true

items.q: He is an honest man.
items.a: I don’t think so!

topics.title: How to give and accept a compliment

items.q: Your cake is really delicious!
items.a: I’m glad you like it!

items.q: You look gorgeous in this outfit. You have a great fashion sense!
items.a: That’s very kind of you to say so.
items.note: gorgeous = beautiful; outfit = clothes set; fashion sense = style

items.q: Your presentation was great!
items.a: Thank you. I really needed that.

items.q: Jill has had a heart attack! She’s just been taken to hospital!
items.a: How awful/terrible!

items.q: My back kills me!
items.a: I’m sorry to hear this!

items.q: I’ve lost one of my gloves.
items.a: What a shame!

items.q: I spent half an hour looking for my car key! When I got to my car, I saw I had a flat tyre.
items.a: I can imagine! Oh, no!
items.note: flat tyre = little air in tyre; frustrating = annoying

topics.title: How to ask to repeat and check understanding

items.q: Are you following me?
items.a: No, you’ve lost me. Could you explain that again, please?

items.q: Are you with me?
items.a: Sorry, what was that again?

items.q: Am I making sense?
items.a: Could you explain that another way/just one more time, please?
items.note: to make sense = to be easy to understand

topics.title: How to finish a conversation and say good-bye

items.q: It was nice to talk to you but I’ve got to go now.
items.a: You too. See you around.

items.q: It was great to see you, but I must dash now.
items.a: It was good to see you too. Take care.
items.note: to dash = go quickly in a hurry

items.q: I should get going.
items.a: Ok. See you later.

items.q: I’m running terribly late!
items.a: Ok. See you around.

items.q: I hope we meet again soon.
items.a: Yes, let’s keep in touch.
items.note: to keep in touch = call/write from time to time

topics.title: How to go to the cinema

items.q: Let’s go to the cinema. What’s on?
items.a: The Martian. Matt Damon is in the film.
items.note: be on = to be shown at the cinema

items.q: Can we have two tickets for The Martian, please?
items.a: That’s 30 euros. Here you are. — Thank you.

items.q: Excuse me, you’re in my seat.
items.a: Sorry? That’s my seat 8 row 15. — Oh, yes, you’re right. Sorry.

topics.title: How to join a fitness club

items.q: What are your hours?
items.a: We’re open from 9 am to 10 pm seven days a week.

items.q: I’d like to sign up for a membership. How much is the charge?
items.a: It’s 80 euros.
items.note: to sign up for = to join

items.q: I’d like to sign up for pilates classes. What days and what time are they?
items.a: They are on Tuesday and Friday at 7 pm. — Great.

items.q: Is this the end of the line?
items.a: No, the end of the line is over there.

items.q: Are you in the line?
items.a: Yeap.

items.q: Could you hold my place in the queue? I should be back right now.
items.a: Sure.
items.note: hold my place = keep spot while away briefly

items.q: Can I sneak ahead of you? I only have one item.
items.a: Yes, go ahead.
items.note: to sneak ahead = be served before someone

items.q: Excuse me, I was here before you. I should be ahead of you in the queue.
items.a: Sorry.

items.q: I’d like to exchange dollars into euros. What’s the exchange rate, please?
items.a: One euro is 1.2 dollar.
items.note: exchange rate = value of one currency to another

items.q: Do you charge a commission?
items.a: Yes, Sir. It’s 2%. — That’s fine. I’d like to exchange 500 euros into dollars.

items.q: How would you like your money?
items.a: In hundred dollar banknotes, please. — That’s 588 dollars.
items.note: banknote = paper money

items.q: I’d like to book a tour of Niagara Falls.
items.a: Yes, of course. We have daily tours available. We’d like to book two adults and a child.
items.note: tour = excursion; adult = grown up

items.q: When does the tour start and when does it finish?
items.a: It starts at 8 am. At 4 pm.

items.q: Where does the tour leave from?
items.a: The bus will pick you up right outside the hotel.
items.note: to pick up = to collect

items.q: I need a taxi to the Louvre. Where from?
items.a: Rue Michel-Ange.

items.q: What time is it for?
items.a: As soon as possible, please.

items.q: How long will it be till it comes?
items.a: 15 minutes.

topics.title: How to ask for and give directions

items.q: How do I get to the Museum of Modern Art?
items.a: Go straight ahead and take the second right. You’ll see the sign for it.
items.note: go straight ahead = same direction

items.q: How do I get to the nearest metro station, please?
items.a: Go down this street till you get to the supermarket. Go past the supermarket and turn left. It’s on your right.

items.q: Is there a bank near here, please?
items.a: Take the right turning at the next traffic light. — So, I take the next left? — No, take the next right.

items.q: Is there a chemist’s near here?
items.a: Follow me. I’ll take you there. — Thank you, that’s very kind.

topics.title: How to get around by bus and metro

items.q: Does this bus go to the city centre?
items.a: No, it doesn’t. You need the 23.

items.q: Does it stop outside the Opera House?
items.a: Yes, it does.

items.q: Can I buy a ticket on the bus?
items.a: No, but you can buy it from a ticket machine over there.

items.q: Is anybody sitting here? / Is this seat taken?
items.a: No, go ahead. / I’m sorry, my wife is sitting here.

items.q: How many stops is it to Central Park?
items.a: It’s 4 stops.

items.q: Where do I get off for the hospital?
items.a: At the next stop.
items.note: to get off = to leave the bus

items.q: How do I get to Bilbao?
items.a: Take the purple line at Ventilla and change at Plaza de Castilla to the light blue line.

items.q: I'd like a ticket to Rome, please.
items.a: A single or return? — A single, please.
items.note: single = one-way ticket; return = round-trip ticket

items.q: Are there any trains leaving tomorrow?
items.a: There are two trains to Rome: 10.20 am and 5 pm. — I'd like the 10.20 train. — Okay, booked for you!

items.q: Great party, isn’t it? I’m Ruth.
items.a: Yeah. It’s cool. I’m Julia. Nice to meet you. — You too.

items.q: Hi, I’m Kevin. So, how do you know the host?
items.a: Hi, Kevin! I’m David. I and Daniel work together. What about you? — I live next door.
items.note: host = person inviting guests; next door = house next to yours

items.q: Laura, meet Seon! Seon, this is Laura!
items.a: Nice to meet you, Seon. — You too, Laura!

items.q: James, this is Chris. Chris, this is James.
items.a: Nice to meet you, James! — You too, Chris. I’ve heard a lot about you! — All good, I hope.

topics.title: How to welcome a new employee

items.q: Hi, I’m Claire. Are you new here?
items.a: Nice to meet you. I’m Robert. Yes, it’s my first day here.

items.q: You must be Susan. I’m Jill. Let me show you around.
items.a: Yes, right. Nice to meet you too, Jill. Thank you.
items.note: show you around = show a place/office

items.q: Hello, Jake. Welcome to the Nesco Company. Let me introduce you to some people.
items.a: Thank you, that would be nice.

items.q: Hi, I’m Jeff. Where will you be working?
items.a: I’m Alex, a new paralegal. On the seventh floor. — We’ll be seeing a lot of each other then.
items.note: paralegal = legal assistant

items.q: Would you like to come to my birthday party at 5 pm?
items.a: I’d love to! I’ll be there. Thanks!

items.q: Would you like to come over for dinner tonight?
items.a: That would be lovely but I’ve got a previous arrangement. I'd love to come another time!
items.note: previous arrangement = earlier plan

items.q: I’d love it if you could come to stay but do you mind dogs?
items.a: No, of course not. Thank you for inviting me.

topics.title: How to welcome guests & compliment home

items.q: Hi, come in! I’m glad you could make it.
items.a: Nice to see you! Thank you for asking me. — It’s a pleasure to have you here.
items.note: make it = manage to get somewhere

items.q: Nice to have you here. How was your journey?
items.a: I hit a traffic jam but quite smooth after all.
items.note: hit a traffic jam = busy traffic; smooth = without problems

items.q: You’ve got a lovely house.
items.a: Thank you. Let me show you around.

items.q: Come into the living room and have a seat. Make yourself comfortable.
items.a: Your living room is very beautiful! Thank you!

topics.title: How to offer drinks & food to guests

items.q: Would you like a drink? / Can I get you something to drink?
items.a: Yes, please. I’d like a cup of tea. / What have you got?

items.q: How do you take your coffee?
items.a: Two sugars, no milk, please.

items.q: Help yourself to the cookies.
items.a: Thank you! They are delicious.
items.note: help yourself = serve yourself food/drink

items.q: Please, go ahead with the salad, I’ll bring the lamb in red wine in a minute.
items.a: Sounds delicious!

items.q: Can I get anyone anything? / Are you done?
items.a: No, thanks. We are full. The meal was delicious. / Yes, thank you.

items.q: Thank you for having us. / Thank you for inviting us.
items.a: We are glad you could come. Have a safe journey. Come back again!

topics.title: How to ask out, date & small talk

items.q: What are you up to today? Would you like to go to the cinema tonight?
items.a: Nothing really. Yeah, what’s on?

items.q: I was thinking... Do you want to meet up for a drink some time?
items.a: Sounds good! What about tomorrow evening?

items.q: I was wondering if you would have dinner with me?
items.a: Dinner? Why not? When? — How about tonight? — Sorry, I can’t make it tonight. Tomorrow is fine.

items.q: Would you like to go out some time?
items.a: That’s nice of you, but I’m already seeing someone.
items.note: seeing someone = in a relationship

items.q: I just thought we could grab a coffee sometime.
items.a: No, sorry. You're a nice guy, but I'm just not into you in that way.
items.note: into someone = interested in them

items.q: Nice day, isn’t it?
items.a: Yeah, it’s lovely outside.

items.q: Can you believe all this rain we’ve been having?
items.a: Yes, we sure have!

items.q: How much do you earn?
items.a: I’d rather not say.
items.note: avoid answering a question politely

items.q: Can we meet on the 16th of July?
items.a: Yes, it suits me perfectly.

items.q: We were going to meet on Friday but something has come up. Can we fix another time?
items.a: Sure. Would Monday be ok?
items.note: come up = a problem arises

topics.title: How to ask for items & buy things

items.q: Hello! Have you got souvenir mugs?
items.a: Yes, we have them here.

items.q: Have you got umbrellas?
items.a: Yes. Are you looking for men’s or ladies’ umbrellas? — A ladies’ one.

items.q: Can I have this calendar, please? How much is it?
items.a: Here you are / There you go. It’s 10 pounds.

items.q: Can I have a carton of milk and a loaf of bread, please?
items.a: Here you are. That’s 4 euros.

items.q: Can I have a box of tissues, please?
items.a: I’m sorry, we are out of tissues.
items.note: out of = no more in stock

items.q: I’m looking for a dishwasher.
items.a: Freestanding or built-in?

items.q: Can I help you?
items.a: No, I am just looking around. — Just let me know if you need anything.

items.q: Excuse me, where can I find flour?
items.a: It’s in aisle 4 next to sugar.
items.note: aisle = passage between shelves

items.q: Where can I weigh my fruit?
items.a: The scales are at the end of the aisle.
items.note: scales = weighing equipment

items.q: Are the bags free of charge?
items.a: Yes, we don’t charge for them.
items.note: free of charge = costing no money

items.q: I’m looking for a pair of trousers. I’m a 40 for trousers.
items.a: What colour are you looking for?

items.q: I’m looking for a pair of shoes. I’m a 9 for shoes.
items.a: What kind of shoes are you looking for? Dress shoes, loafers, oxfords?
items.note: loafers = casual shoes; oxfords = formal shoes

items.q: What’s this dress made of? Can it be machine washed?
items.a: Pure wool. No, the care instructions say it has to be washed by hand.
items.note: pure wool = sheep hair; care instructions = washing rules

items.q: Where are the changing/fitting rooms? Can I try these jeans on?
items.a: Over there. Sure, the changing rooms are over there.
items.note: try on = put on clothes to see fit

items.q: Does the dress fit?
items.a: No, it’s too tight. Do you have it in a bigger size? — Here you are. — This one is ok, I’ll take it.

items.q: Are the trousers ok?
items.a: They are too big. Do you have them in a smaller size? — No, I’m afraid not. — I’ll leave them then.
items.note: leave them = not buy

items.q: Is this shirt in the sale? How long does the sale last?
items.a: Yes, it’s 30% off. It ends next Sunday.
items.note: 30% off = price reduced

items.q: Are you in the tax-free shopping scheme? How much to qualify for a VAT refund?
items.a: Yes, Sir. Can I see your passport? The minimum amount is 175 euros.
items.note: VAT return = tax refund for tourists

items.q: Can I pay by credit card? / Do you take credit cards?
items.a: Yes, please enter your PIN. / No, I’m afraid we don’t. Cash only.

items.q: Do you have a refund policy?
items.a: Yes, you have to keep the receipt and bring an item back within 2 weeks.
items.note: receipt = proof of payment; refund policy = return rules

items.q: I’d like to return this skirt. The stitching is coming undone.
items.a: Sure. Can I have your receipt, please?
items.note: stitching coming undone = threads untied

items.q: I’d like to return these trousers. They shrank a lot after I washed them.
items.a: What seems to be the problem? Did you follow the care instructions?
items.note: shrink = become smaller

items.q: How much is it? 30 euros. That’s pretty steep. Can you knock a few dollars off?
items.a: Ok. You can have it for 28.
items.note: steep = expensive; knock off = reduce price

items.q: How much is this vase? 100 euros. How about 70 euros?
items.a: You can have it for 85. — I’m afraid that’s still too much.

items.q: How much are these gloves? 30 dollars. Will you take 20 for them?
items.a: 25 is the best price.

title: Air Travel
sub: Booking Flights, Check-in, Security, Customs & Luggage

topics.title: How to book & change a flight

items.q: What flights are there to Oslo?
items.a: There are two flights tomorrow: 7.30 am and 4 pm.

items.q: Are there any direct flights to Dallas?
items.a: No, you'll have to transfer either in Chicago or Kansas City.
items.note: transfer = change planes

items.q: I’d like to book a flight to Beijing, please. The 19th of March.
items.a: There is a flight at 5.20 am. Would you like to be booked on it? — Yes, please.

items.q: I’d like to change my flight reservation. I'm booked on flight XPL on April 12.
items.a: What date would you like to depart? Will you have to pay a change fee? Yes, booked over 24h ago.
items.note: fee = service charge; depart = leave

items.q: Can I see your passport and tickets, please?
items.a: Here you are. Your flight has been delayed. It's scheduled to depart at 4.30 pm.
items.note: delayed = later than planned; scheduled = planned

items.q: Would you like an aisle or a window seat?
items.a: A window seat, please.
items.note: aisle seat = seat near passage

items.q: Are you checking in any bags?
items.a: I have a suitcase to check and one carry-on. — This exceeds size restrictions. Put it on the carry-on sizer.
items.note: carry-on = bag taken onto plane

items.q: Did you pack your bags yourself? Are there any sharp or prohibited items?
items.a: Yes, I did. No.
items.note: prohibited = banned; sharp = able to cut

items.q: I have a stopover in Miami. Will I have to collect my luggage there?
items.a: No, your luggage will go straight through to Montevideo. Here is your boarding pass.
items.note: stopover = flight break; collect = pick up

items.q: Do I need to take my mobile out of the bag?
items.a: Yes, you do. Put it into the bin, please.
items.note: bin = plastic tray/container

items.q: Do you have any coins or keys in your pockets?
items.a: No, I’ve taken everything out. — Then walk through the body scan.

items.q: Can I take this bottle of water on board?
items.a: No, I’m afraid not, Sir.
items.note: on board = on the aircraft

items.q: Is this the gate for flight 234 to Madrid?
items.a: Yes, it is.

items.q: Welcome to the USA. Where are you travelling from and what is the purpose of your trip?
items.a: From France. I’m here on holiday for 10 days.
items.note: purpose = reason for travel

items.q: Who are you travelling with and where will you be staying?
items.a: With my husband. At the Hilton Hotel.

items.q: My luggage hasn’t arrived. I think it’s lost. What does your bag look like?
items.a: It’s a brown suitcase with my name on it. — It is being held by customs in that corridor.

items.q: I picked up my suitcase and found that it’s been damaged.
items.a: What’s the problem? — The wheel is broken and the side is dented.
items.note: dented = hollow on surface

items.q: Hello! Are you Ms. Jones? Welcome to Brazil.
items.a: Yes, I am. I’m Sanches from Netco. I’m here to take you to our office.

items.q: Did you have a good flight? You must be very tired.
items.a: It was good but very long. Yes, I really am. My car is this way.

items.q: I’d like to rent a car for 3 days. What type of car would you like?
items.a: I’d like a midsize car. How much would it cost? — 30 dollars per day.

items.q: Would you like insurance on your car? How many people are going to drive?
items.a: Yes, please. Just myself.
items.note: insurance = protects costs if accident happens

items.q: Can I see your driver’s licence?
items.a: Will my international licence do?

items.q: Do I have to return the car to this location?
items.a: No, you can leave it at any of our locations. Return it by 2 am on Wednesday.

items.q: How much would you charge me if I’m an hour late?
items.a: There is a late return fee.
items.note: charge = request payment

items.q: I’m calling about the flat for rent. Is it still available? Can I see it today?
items.a: Yes, it is.

items.q: How much is the rent? Are utilities included?
items.a: It’s 1200 dollars per month. No, you’ll have to pay utilities yourself.
items.note: utilities = gas, water, electricity

items.q: When is the rent due?
items.a: On the first of each month. It’s paid in advance.
items.note: due = must be paid; in advance = before time

items.q: Will the rent go up?
items.a: Not until the end of the lease. When your lease expires the rent may go up.
items.note: lease = rental contract; expire = end

items.q: How much is the security deposit?
items.a: It’s a month’s rent.
items.note: security deposit = returned when you move out

items.q: Can I sublet? How much notice do I need to give if I want to leave early?
items.a: Yes, with written permission. You need to give a month’s notice.
items.note: sublet = rent to another; notice = advance notification

items.q: Who do I contact if there is a problem? When will the flat be available?
items.a: Me, here is my phone number. Available next month.

items.q: How much is a room? Are your basic rooms en suite?
items.a: From $50 to $250 for a suite. Basic single has shared facilities; others are en-suite.
items.note: en-suite = room with private bathroom; suite = set of rooms

items.q: I need a room for 3 people (one double bed and one single bed).
items.a: Yes, we have suites for three people.

items.q: Is breakfast included? Do you have free wi-fi?
items.a: Local cafe offers guest discounts. Wi-fi is free of charge throughout hotel.

items.q: What are your check-in and check-out times? What is your cancellation policy?
items.a: Check-in 2 pm, check-out 12 pm. Cancel at least 24h before to avoid fee.

items.q: I’d like to book a double room for three nights starting Monday the 9th.
items.a: Who is the booking for? — Victoria Garcia. Are you going to put a hold on my card?
items.note: put a hold = reserve funds on card

items.q: Hello, I’m checking in. My name is Julia Lawrence.
items.a: Yes, Ms. Lawrence... Single room for 5 nights. Is that right? — Yes, that’s right.

items.q: Are you still open for breakfast?
items.a: Yes, but the restaurant closes soon, so you’d better hurry.

items.q: What time is dinner served? When does breakfast start?
items.a: Dinner is from 6 pm to 9 pm. Breakfast starts at 7.30 am.

items.q: What time does the pool open? Do I have to bring my own towel?
items.a: Opens at 6.30 am. You can get a towel at the pool.

items.q: Can you send laundry service up to room 236, please?
items.a: Yes, I’ll send someone up right away.

items.q: Can I have my suit pressed?
items.a: We have an ironing room equipped with iron and board on the 2nd floor.
items.note: press = iron smooth

items.q: My room is noisy. Could I move to a quieter one?
items.a: Let me just check if there are any rooms available now.

items.q: I just checked into my room and there’s hair in the bathtub.
items.a: I’m sorry. I’ll send up someone from housekeeping right now.
items.note: housekeeping = cleaning department

items.q: The air conditioner isn’t working / The bulb isn't working.
items.a: I’ll call maintenance / get someone to replace it right away.
items.note: maintenance = repairs team

items.q: The toilet is not flushing properly.
items.a: I’ll send the plumber in right away.
items.note: flush = pass water through toilet; plumber = toilet/pipe repairer

items.q: The mini bar is empty. Could you get someone to restock it?
items.a: Sure.

items.q: I am checking out of room 451. Could I have my bill, please?
items.a: Yes, here it is. How would you like to pay? Settle on card on file?
items.note: card on file = registered banking card

items.q: Can I leave my suitcase with the hotel for 2 days?
items.a: Yes, of course. We will hold your suitcase free of charge.

items.q: I’d like to make an appointment with a GP, please.
items.a: When would you like to come?
items.note: GP = General Practitioner (family doctor)

items.q: I’d like to make an appointment with Dr. Taylor, please?
items.a: Dr. Taylor is booked up today but tomorrow at 3 pm is possible. — That’s fine.
items.note: booked up = busy with no time available

items.q: Can I make an appointment with the dentist, please?
items.a: Tomorrow at 10 am or 3.30 pm. Which time works best for you? — 10 am is ok.

items.q: Would 5.30 pm be ok with you? Do you have anything earlier?
items.a: No, I’m afraid not. If an earlier booking cancels, could you let me know?

items.q: What seems to be the trouble?
items.a: I have blotches all over my body. — Have you eaten anything you are allergic to?
items.note: blotches = red skin marks; allergic = bad reaction to food

items.q: What seems to be the trouble?
items.a: I have a pain in my knee. — What were you doing when the pain started?

items.q: What seems to be the trouble?
items.a: I have a fever and a splitting headache. — Have you been taking any medicine for it?
items.note: splitting headache = severe head pain; fever = high temperature

items.q: What seems to be the trouble?
items.a: Could you describe the pain? Sharp? Mild? Persistent or intermittent?
items.note: persistent = continuous; intermittent = stopping and starting

items.q: I’ll prescribe you a cream. You should apply it twice a day.
items.a: How long will the swelling take to go down? — About a week.
items.note: prescribe = order medicine; swelling = swollen area

items.q: You should go to the hospital for some blood tests / X-ray.
items.a: Do you think I've torn my joint, doctor? — If you are not better in two days, come see me.
items.note: joint = bone junction; X-ray = scan

title: Eating Out
sub: Reserving, Ordering, Special Requests & The Bill

items.q: I’d like to book a table for tonight, please. For 4 people at 7 pm.
items.a: Good. I have you reserved for a table for 4 at 7 pm.

items.q: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
items.a: Yes, a table for two in the name of Johnson. / I'm joining Tom Jenkin's party.

items.q: Do you have a booking? / Have you got any free tables?
items.a: No, we don’t. Is there a table free? — You’ll have to wait about 10 minutes.

items.q: Can we have a table by the window / on the terrace?
items.a: Yes, of course. / I’ll see if there is one free.

items.q: Do you have a high chair for little children?
items.a: Sure. I’ll get it for you.

items.q: What should I order? What’s best here?
items.a: They serve delicious fish here. Their speciality is seafood.
items.note: speciality = signature dish

items.q: Are you ready to order? Can I take your order?
items.a: Yes, I’ll have tuna salad and a bottle of still water, please.
items.note: still water = without bubbles

items.q: Could you serve the salad on the side, please? What dressings do you have?
items.a: Sure. We have Italian, French, and blue cheese.
items.note: on the side = on a separate dish

items.q: How would you like your steak done? Rare, medium, well-done?
items.a: Medium, please. We are in a hurry. How long will it take? — About 10 minutes.
items.note: rare = lightly cooked

items.q: Would you like a dessert? Is there anything you would recommend?
items.a: Tiramisu. It’s delicious.

topics.title: Requests, Meal issues & Paying the bill

items.q: Excuse me, I dropped my fork. Can I get another, please?
items.a: Sure. I’ll get you one right away.

items.q: Excuse me, this cup is dirty. / There’s a hair in the soup.
items.a: I apologize. I’ll bring you another one / We won’t charge you for the soup.

items.q: My baked potato is raw inside. / This meat is undercooked.
items.a: Sorry, Mam. I’ll replace it with a well-baked one right away.
items.note: raw = not cooked; undercooked = cooked insufficiently

items.q: Let’s split it.
items.a: No, I’ll get it. It’s my treat. / No, it’s on me. — Thank you.
items.note: split = divide evenly; my treat / on me = I will pay

items.q: Can I have the bill, please? We’d like separate bills.
items.a: Coming right up. Sure.

items.q: I’m afraid there is a mistake in the bill. You charged me twice for dessert.
items.a: I’m sorry, Mam. I’ll bring you the correct bill right away.

title: Solving Problems & Emergencies
sub: Appliances, Car Trouble, Health & Police Reports

items.q: The washing machine isn’t working. Do you know what’s wrong with it?
items.a: The remote control isn’t working. The batteries might have run out.

items.q: My lock is broken. The key doesn’t turn.
items.a: You should call the locksmith.
items.note: locksmith = person who repairs locks

items.q: The tap in the kitchen is dripping.
items.a: I’ll send the plumber in right now.
items.note: drip = water falling in small drops

items.q: One of my burners won’t light. / The bulb is blown.
items.a: It can be clogged. Just clean it. / I’ll replace it right now.
items.note: clogged = blocked; blown = filament burned out

items.q: I’ve locked myself out of my car.
items.a: Have you got the second key?
items.note: keys locked inside car

items.q: My car won’t start. The battery must be dead.
items.a: Do you need a boost? / You’d better call the garage quick.
items.note: boost = jump-start battery with cables

items.q: Your right brake light is out. / My car tyre is flat.
items.a: Thanks for telling me. / Does it have a puncture?
items.note: puncture = small hole in tyre

items.q: The man has fallen over and badly hurt himself.
items.a: He should be taken to the fracture clinic.
items.note: fracture clinic = clinic for broken bones

items.q: The woman has fainted in the heat. She is unconscious.
items.a: Call an ambulance. She needs CPR.
items.note: faint = lose consciousness; CPR = chest compression resuscitation

items.q: I’ve burned myself. It’s my hand.
items.a: Put your hand under cold water.

items.q: There is a robbery in progress / fight outside the bar.
items.a: What’s the address? Hold on, I’ll get the police dispatched.
items.note: dispatched = sent

items.q: There’s a car accident. Is anyone trapped inside?
items.a: One man is. The ambulance is on the way. What should we do until they arrive?

items.q: My house is on fire! / My house is flooding!
items.a: The fire crew is on its way. / Have you got a burst pipe?
items.note: burst pipe = broken water pipe

items.q: I’d like to report a crime / break-in. My bag has been stolen.
items.a: Can you tell me what happened? When and where did it happen?
items.note: break-in = illegal entry into house/car

title: Telephoning
sub: Calling, Leaving Messages, Timing & Connection Issues

items.q: Can I speak to Mary Taylor, please?
items.a: Speaking. — Hi, Mary. It’s Rita Cooper.

items.q: Could I speak to Peter Wright, please? Who is calling?
items.a: It’s Brian Evans. — Hold on while I get him.

items.q: Hi, Brian. How are you doing? What can I do for you?
items.a: I’m calling to remind you of our dinner plans.
items.note: remind = make someone remember

items.q: Can I speak to someone from the HR department? Can I ask what it is in connection with?
items.a: I’m calling about applying for the job of a sales representative. — I’ll connect you.

items.q: She is at lunch. Would you like to leave a message or call her back later?
items.a: I’ll call her back, thanks. / Can I take a message? — Yes, please. I'll get a pen.

items.q: He isn’t at his desk now. Is it urgent?
items.a: No, not really. Can I just leave a message for him, please?
items.note: urgent = needs immediate action

items.q: Is this a good time to call?
items.a: Sure. Now is fine. What’s up? / Look, I'm in the middle of something. Could you call back in a couple of hours?

items.q: He is in a meeting. Do you know when it’ll be over?
items.a: Do you know how long he’ll be?
items.note: to be over = to finish

items.q: The line is bad. Can you speak up?
items.a: I’ll try calling you when I’m in the office.
items.note: speak up = speak louder

items.q: My phone is dying. I’m afraid we’ll get cut off now.
items.a: Let me call you on the other phone.
items.note: phone is dying = battery running out; cut off = disconnected
